activity_context.topic_title: Velocity and Acceleration for Plane Motion

feedback.problem: A particle moves with constant acceleration. When $t=0\,\text{s},$ the velocity of the particle is $(5i+j)\,\text{ft/s},$ and when $t=4\,\text{s},$ the velocity of the particle is $(5i+13j)\,\text{ft/s}.$ Calculate the acceleration of the particle.
feedback.worked_solution:
Recall that when a particle moves with constant acceleration, the velocity vector at time $t$ can be found using

$$
v=u+at,
$$

where $u$ is the initial velocity, and $a$ is the acceleration of the particle.

Substituting 

$$
u=5i+j,\,v=5i+13j,\,t=4,
$$

into the equation above, we can solve for $a,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =u+at \\ 5i+13j & =(5i+j)+a(4) \\ 12j & =4a \\ a & =\frac{1}{4}(12j) \\  & =3j\,{\text{ft/s}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
